summary: People call it "delightfully captivating," and that lands because the movie turns teenage awkwardness, band-kid invention, and eighties pop longing into a real good mood.
good_pick_if: you want something buoyant, earnest, and easy to root for
maybe_skip_if: you want something sharper or less openly heartfelt

summary: One reviewer says "being modern is almost a slur," which is exactly the joke here: a precise, playful comedy where every gadget and layout choice becomes a sight gag.
good_pick_if: you want a gentle comedy built from design, rhythm, and observation
maybe_skip_if: you want punchlines, speed, or a louder style of funny

source_quotes.text: being modern is almost a slur

summary: People keep calling it an "emotionally layered satire," which is why it lands for groups: funny enough to keep moving, but never so glib that it loses the ache underneath.
good_pick_if: you want something funny, tender, and a little risky in tone
maybe_skip_if: you want historical material handled without tonal swings

summary: One review calls it a "darkly comic criminal caper," and that is the clean pitch: fast-talking chaos, ridiculous character entrances, and a movie that somehow keeps every plate spinning.
good_pick_if: you want a loud, funny crime movie with constant motion
maybe_skip_if: you want emotional depth or room to breathe

summary: People describe it as an "endlessly enjoyable result," which fits the blend perfectly: flirtation, suspense, and just enough old-school sparkle to make the whole thing glide.
good_pick_if: you want a stylish mystery that stays breezy without going weightless
maybe_skip_if: you want something rougher or less polished

summary: A recent review saying it felt like "an all timer 10 minutes in" gets at the appeal: talky, anxious, and sharply romantic in a way that still feels very alive.
good_pick_if: you want smart dialogue, messy chemistry, and workplace tension
maybe_skip_if: you want broad comedy or a less verbal movie night

source_quotes.text: I was already pretty certain this was an all timer 10 minutes in.

summary: People still point to its "gift for uproarious comedy" because the movie is unusually good at being funny and morally corrosive in the same breath.
good_pick_if: you want a sharp talky drama-comedy with real existential bite
maybe_skip_if: you want cleaner heroes or lighter stakes

source_quotes.source: Letterboxd review by Ian Anthony Brownell

summary: One reviewer says Heidi Schreck "does something special here," and that is the pitch: personal, funny, and built to turn a civics argument into a live-wire group watch.
good_pick_if: you want something smart, human, and likely to start a conversation
maybe_skip_if: you want escapism or less overtly political material

source_quotes.text: Heidi Schreck does something special here.

summary: People call it "entirely charming," and that is really the whole sell: storybook framing, runaway-kid sincerity, and a melancholy that never dulls the whimsy.
good_pick_if: you want something sweet, stylized, and gently off-center
maybe_skip_if: you want realism or less deliberate design

summary: That "I don't really do it" line still hits because the movie is so good at turning stalled-twenties panic into something loose, funny, and a little bruised.
good_pick_if: you want a hangout movie with real vulnerability under the jokes
maybe_skip_if: you want neat character growth or higher stakes
